steps.explanationAfterStep: The positive oxygen pulls the π electrons towards itself, so the carbonyl carbon becomes much more electrophilic.
Five- and six-membered rings form easily because the nucleophile is held close to the carbonyl carbon. The new ring oxygen carries the positive charge.
H₃O⁺ is regenerated: the acid is a catalyst. Glucose exists mainly as a six-membered cyclic hemiacetal for the same reason.

title: Cyclic hemiacetal formation
subtitle: 5-Hydroxypentanal closes to a six-membered ring under acid catalysis
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 6

oxonium.caption: protonated cyclic hemiacetal + water
hintTiers: The ring oxygen is positive and carries a proton. Which base is nearby?
Water's lone pair takes that proton, and the O–H bonding pair returns to the ring oxygen. Two arrows.
Water oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton on the ring oxygen; that O–H bond → lone pair on the ring oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Opening the ring just reverses the last step. Remove the proton from the positive ring oxygen instead.
That OH group is neutral and not acidic. The proton to remove is on the positive ring oxygen.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: water takes the proton. Where does the O–H bonding pair go?

reactants.caption: 5-hydroxypentanal + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: An alcohol is a weak nucleophile. How can the acid make the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic?
The carbonyl oxygen takes a proton from H₃O⁺, and that O–H bonding pair stays on water's oxygen. Two arrows.
Carbonyl oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to a proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → lone pair on water's oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: First activate the aldehyde with acid.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The hydroxyl group can add to the neutral aldehyde, but slowly. With acid present, protonate the carbonyl oxygen first: that makes the carbonyl carbon far more electrophilic.
Protonating the hydroxyl group does not help it attack. Protonate the carbonyl oxygen, so that the carbonyl carbon becomes more electrophilic.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the carbonyl oxygen takes the proton. Where does the O–H bonding pair of H₃O⁺ go?

protonated.caption: protonated aldehyde + water
hintTiers: The protonated carbonyl carbon is very electrophilic. Which nucleophile is in the same molecule?
The hydroxyl oxygen bonds to the carbonyl carbon, closing a six-membered ring. The C=O π pair moves onto the positive oxygen. Two arrows.
Hydroxyl oxygen lone pair → new O–C bond to the carbonyl carbon; C=O π bond → lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Water could add, giving the hydrate. But the hydroxyl group in the same molecule is held close by: six-membered rings form fast.
The C=O π electrons move towards the positive oxygen, not onto carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the hydroxyl oxygen attacks. The carbonyl carbon now has five bonds: move the C=O π pair.

mechanismSummary: H₃O⁺ protonates the carbonyl oxygen, making the carbonyl carbon much more electrophilic. The hydroxyl group at the other end of the chain attacks it, closing a six-membered ring, and water removes the proton from the ring oxygen, regenerating H₃O⁺.
